case_title: Ramji Singh & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Political rival (village Pradhan election); prior dispute over cultivation of a plot; relations strained, belonging to different groups. No family relationship between the accused and the victim is described.
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.147, 148, 149, 302, 449 (charged); s.452 IPC also recorded in the FIR
weapon: Firearms (two guns, three shots each fired by two accused); axes; pitchfork (kanta); lathi
evidence_type: Eyewitness (two eyewitnesses); medical (post-mortem); documentary (written complaint/FIR); scribe witness; site plan; ballistic/seized guns (not proved)
aggravating_circumstances: Armed group of six attacking in broad daylight; two accused used guns; threats to bystanders to prevent intervention.
high_court_outcome: Appeal by the State allowed; trial court acquittal set aside; accused Ramji Singh (A-2), Laxman Singh (A-4) and Lala Ram (A-5) convicted under ss.147, 148, 302/149 IPC and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.10,000 each; appeal against A-1, A-3, A-6 abated on their death.
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 r/w s.149 (murder by unlawful assembly), with s.147 and s.148 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that the victim had a dispute with one of the accused over the cultivation of a plot of land, which led to an exchange of abuses and threats that the victim would be killed. Later the same day, around noon, the victim sat on a cot in the courtyard of another villager's house while the victim's uncle went to get an agricultural implement repaired. The uncle heard a noise and returned to find six accused standing outside the house, armed with a lathi, two guns, two axes and a pitchfork. One accused allegedly directed that the victim be killed. Two accused fired three shots each from the entrance of the house, two others struck the victim with axes, and another struck with a pitchfork. The victim died on the spot. Other villagers arrived, and the accused threatened them before running away. The uncle dictated a written complaint immediately afterwards. It was scribed by a teacher who reached the spot around 12:45 pm, and was taken to the police station and registered as a first information report. The post-mortem doctor recorded six firearm entry wounds, several incised wounds and firearm exit wounds, and opined that death occurred between 12 and 12:30 pm. The investigation included a site plan and the seizure of guns. The ballistic report was not proved. Two eyewitnesses gave evidence supporting the prosecution account.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from six firearm entry wounds, axe and pitchfork injuries (incised wounds) and firearm exit wounds.
number_of_offences: 5 charged (ss.147, 148, 149, 302, 449 IPC); 3 finally upheld for the appellants (ss.147, 148, 302/149 IPC)
motive: alleged: dispute over cultivation of a plot of land and rivalry arising from village Pradhan election; the court assumed enmity existed but did not decide motive.
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of two eyewitnesses (PW-1 and PW-2), corroborated by the scribe (PW-4); the written complaint recorded immediately after the occurrence and the FIR based on it; medical evidence matching firearm and sharp-edged injuries and time of death.
witness_credibility: The eyewitnesses' statements were almost identical with no major contradictions; PW-2 may have slightly improved his version but the core remained intact; enmity and interest did not make them unreliable; PW-4 found to be independent and not discredited.
post_offence_conduct: Threatened bystanders not to interfere and fled the scene.
trial_duration: offence: 17.06.1982; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 30.04.2014; Supreme Court: 11.12.2019
legal_representation: Appellants: Rajiv Dutta and Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Advs., with others. State of UP: Ms. Sansriti Pathak and Krishnanand Pandeya, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No.66/82); investigation completed; charge sheet filed against all six accused; trial completed in Sessions Court.
procedural_irregularity: Delay in compliance with s.157 CrPC not proved and noted as not fatal; ballistic report not proved and bullets not all sent for examination (court held this did not discredit eyewitnesses).
appeal_history: Trial court: all accused acquitted. High Court: acquittal set aside; three appellants convicted under ss.147, 148, 302/149 IPC, life imprisonment. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Trial court's view was perverse; medical and ocular evidence consistent; FIR time correctly recorded; all material witnesses examined.
defence_argument: Medical evidence renders eyewitness presence doubtful; contradictions in witnesses; witnesses related to deceased and interested; FIR ante-timed; material witnesses not examined; ballistic report not proved.
legal_principle_applied: Enmity between parties is not by itself sufficient to discredit eyewitnesses; each case decided on its own evidence; site plan is not to scale and cannot fix exact directions; ocular evidence corroborated by medical evidence prevails over investigative lapses.
precedent_relied_upon: Meharaj Singh (L/NK) v. State of U.P., (1994) 5 SCC 188 (cited by appellants; held inapplicable)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Attack by six heavily armed persons, two with guns, in broad daylight; threats to bystanders intimidating witnesses.
